scope: Full website arc after syncing live main: protect The Desk's sourced claims, clear the article performance gate, verify staging, then commit, push and deploy production.

items.title: Extract publisher article prose before selecting sourced facts
items.why: The current fetcher flattens the full HTML page. The 2026-09-28 edition cites TechCrunch navigation, event promotion and related-story links as facts even though the article has an entry-content body.
items.outcome: Readers and AI agents can follow fact links to article prose that actually supports the Desk story.
items.recipe: Select a semantic article or article-body container before text extraction, retain the publisher-owned feed fallback for inaccessible pages, and pin the observed TechCrunch shape in the source-fetch self-test.

premises.claim: The source fetcher flattens the full response body

evidence.interpretation: The publisher page has an entry-content article body; the current edition contains four page-chrome facts across two stories.
evidence.limitations: The extraction must fall back safely for publishers without recognizable semantic containers.

L1.recipe: Exclude the observed page chrome from fact selection.

L2.recipe: Extract semantic article bodies with a conservative fallback and test the current publisher shape plus an ordinary article.

L3.recipe: Add a publisher-shape fixture corpus and measure usable sourced-fact yield before and after.

executionLog.note: Article-body extraction now selects semantic publisher prose before fact candidates, excludes sidebars and photo captions, falls back for non-semantic pages, and passes 120/120 self-tests. The saved publisher article yielded two body facts without related-story or event chrome.

items.title: Correct the current edition and gate page-chrome facts before publication
items.why: Fact parity proves byte agreement between corpus and rendered receipts, but it does not reject a source sentence that is actually a related-story link, photo caption or conference advertisement.
items.outcome: The current public edition presents only supported evidence, and future editions fail before a navigation snippet becomes a cited claim.
items.recipe: Remove the four page-chrome facts from the 2026-09-28 day artifact, regenerate its derived claims and pages, and add a focused editorial fact-quality gate with negative controls for valid article sentences.

premises.claim: The current day artifact includes publisher navigation as a fact
premises.pattern: Anthony Ha 11 hours ago In Brief

evidence.interpretation: Four bad facts were read directly from the current day artifact. Each story retains at least two article-sourced facts after removing them.
evidence.limitations: The gate should detect structural page chrome without rejecting legitimate prose containing an event date or a person's name.

L1.recipe: Correct the four facts and regenerate the rendered edition.

L2.recipe: Correct the edition and add a corpus quality gate with positive and negative fixtures.

L3.recipe: Audit the recent corpus for the same failure shape and publish a bounded correction receipt.

executionLog.note: Corrected two related-story facts, removed two event-promotion facts and a photo caption, regenerated the merged 81-story Desk artifacts, and added source-page-chrome checks. Copy quality and claim parity pass; the checker passes 49/49 self-tests. Postbuild now regenerates public Desk stats after the edition changes.

items.title: Clear the article's existing 0.90 Lighthouse performance floor
items.why: Four recent PR Lighthouse runs fail at the article route; the latest scored 0.88 with a 3,901 ms Largest Contentful Paint. The S364 release exception was limited to that release, and the threshold remains 0.90.
items.outcome: A reader reaches the article hero sooner under mobile throttling, and the existing CI floor passes without lowering it.
items.recipe: Measure the article's Largest Contentful Paint request and render path, optimize the proven bottleneck in the article generator or assets, then verify the unchanged 0.90 gate on the candidate.

premises.claim: The article is held to the analytics 0.90 floor

evidence.interpretation: Earlier GitHub runs measured article performance at 0.85–0.88 against the unchanged 0.90 floor. Browser inspection then showed offscreen illustration requests competing with the text LCP. After moving the illustration below sources, GitHub run 36629194379 passed both local-preview and staging Lighthouse gates.
evidence.limitations: A single green candidate does not prove future lab-score stability; monitor the next three article runs.

L1.recipe: Prioritize the LCP hero request from the document head.

L2.recipe: Measure the throttled request path, prioritize the true LCP resource and verify mobile CI without moving the floor.

L3.recipe: Reduce render blocking article CSS if request priority alone does not clear the floor, with seven-theme visual parity.

executionLog.note: Added an early high-priority AVIF hero preload on real-art story pages after a local trace identified the hero as the LCP element. A new hosted Lighthouse run must confirm the unchanged 0.90 floor.

Moved article illustration and reactions below the story and sources after hosted traces showed below-the-fold art competing with the text LCP. Verified no art request in the first mobile viewport, 168/168 reviewed theme captures, 215/215 mobile checks, and Lighthouse run 36629194379 passing the unchanged local and staging floors.

rejectedCandidates: Membership/auth changes have standing provider and acceptance holds and no new verified premise in this arc.
Gamification and feedback-loop expansion lack a measured current reader need and would distract from sourced-claim quality.
Token/API reduction has no measured cost hotspot in the current content lane.
